Rashi on Shabbat 54a:10:1.hebrew: ולא יקשור גמלים זו לזו וימשוך - האחד, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:10:1.english: And one may not tie camels one to another and pull - [He pulls] the one [lead camel], as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:10:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יכרוך - החבלים בכרך אחד, ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:10:2.english: Provided that he does not intertwine - The ropes into a single bundle; and in the Gemara the reason is explained.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:1.hebrew: בזנבו ובחוטרתו - דכיון דקשורה בשניהם, לא נפלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:1.english: To its tail and to its hump - For since it is tied to both of them, it does not fall.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:2.hebrew: חוטרתו - חלדרוב"א, שיש לכל גמלים על גביהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:2.english: Its hump - Haldrobe [in Old French, a hump], which all camels have on their backs.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:3.hebrew: בשלייתה - דכיון דכאיב, לא מנתחא לי'. ול"נ: מטולטלת — כר קטן מלא מוכין נותנין לו תחת הזנב, כדי שלא תשחית הרצועה הבשר; לפי שהמשוי שעל גבה, כשהגמל יורד, מכביד ויורד כלפי צוארה, אלא שהרצועה מעכבתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:11:3.english: [Tied] to its afterbirth - For since it is painful, she will not detach it. And it seems to me: A metulthelet is a small cushion filled with padding [that] they place under its tail, so that the strap does not damage the flesh; for the load that is on its back, when the camel descends [a slope], bears down and slides toward its neck, but the strap holds it back.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:12:1.english: Foreleg and hind leg - He binds one of the forelegs and one of the hind legs together.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:12:2.hebrew: יד על גב זרועו - אחד מידיו כופף כלפי מעלה וקושר, כדי שלא יהו לו אלא ג' רגלים לברוח:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:12:2.english: [A] foreleg upon its upper foreleg - One bends one of its forelegs upward and ties [it], so that it will have only three legs to run away.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:13:1.hebrew: שתי ידים - כאחד, או שתי רגלים כאחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:13:1.english: Two forelegs - [Bound] together, or two hind legs [bound] together.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:14:1.english: And still it is not similar - This Tanna to [the statement of] Rav Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:14:2.hebrew: רישא וסיפא ניחא - כדרב יהודה. אבל מציעתא, דקתני "או שתי ידים או שתי רגלים", קשיא לדרב יהודה, דלא קרי עקוד אלא יד ורגל, כיצחק בן אברהם, דכתיב (בראשית כב) "ויעקד" — כפף ידיו ורגליו לאחוריו, וקשר יד ורגל יחד, ונפשט צוארו לאחוריו:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:14:2.english: The first clause and the last clause work out well - In accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Yehuda. But the middle clause, which teaches "either two forelegs or two hind legs," is difficult for Rav Yehuda, who does not call [an animal] "bound" [akud] unless [it is tied] foreleg and hind leg, like Isaac, son of Abraham, as it is written (Genesis 22:9): "And he bound [Isaac]" — he bent his hands and feet behind him, and tied hand and foot together, and his neck was extended backward.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:16:1.hebrew: לחינגא - לשוק, למוכרם. חינגא — ע"ש שסובבין את השוק מחולות מחולות, עגולות של בני אדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:16:1.english: To the market [ḥinga] - To the market, to sell them. Ḥinga [is so named] because they encircle the market in dance circles, circular [groups] of people.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:17:1.hebrew: לענין כלאים שנוי - האי שלא יכרוך דמתני' — לא שייך ביה איסור שבת, אלא משום כלאים אסר ליה, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:17:1.english: It was taught with regard to diverse kinds - This [clause], "provided that he does not intertwine," of the Mishnah — the prohibition of Shabbat does not apply to it; rather, [the Tanna] prohibited it because of diverse kinds, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:17:2.hebrew: אי נימא כלאים דאדם - דכי כריך להן סביבות ידו, נמצא קשור עם הגמלים; ופעמים שהן מושכין שום דבר, ונמצא אדם וגמל מנהיגין יחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:17:2.english: If we say diverse kinds of man - For when he wraps them around his hand, he turns out to be tied with the camels; and at times they pull something, and it turns out that a man and a camel are leading [it] together.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:1.hebrew: כלאים דחבלים - שיש בהן חבלי צמר וחבלי פשתן, וכי כריך להו הוו כלאים, וידו מתחממת באחיזתן, וקסבר: דבר שאין מתכוין אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:1.english: Diverse kinds of ropes - That among them are woolen ropes and linen ropes, and when he wraps them [around his hand], they become diverse kinds, and his hand is warmed by holding them, and he holds [that] an unintentional act is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:2.hebrew: והתנן אדם מותר עם כולם - עם כל הבהמות, לחרוש ולמשוך, שלא אסרה תורה אלא שני מיני בהמה יחד, כעין שור וחמור. ומשנה זו במסכת כלאים:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:2.english: And didn't we learn: A person is permitted with all of them - With all animals, to plow and to pull, for the Torah forbade only two species of animals together, like an ox and a donkey. And this mishna is in Tractate Kilayim.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:3.english: One who attaches - [That is, one who attaches] garments of wool and linen.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:4.hebrew: בתכיפה אחת - כגון ע"י מחט פעם אחת, או שקשר קשר אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:4.english: With a single stitch - Such as by means of a needle one time, or where he tied a single knot:

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:5.hebrew: אינו חיבור - דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:י״א) צמר ופשתים יחדו, לא אסרה התורה אלא חבור יפה המתקיים:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:18:5.english: It is not a connection - As it is written: (Deuteronomy 22:11) “Wool and linen together” — the Torah prohibited only a proper, lasting connection.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:19:1.english: Intertwining and tying - [Is equivalent to fastening] with two stitches.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:1:1.english: Attire of a harlot - [It is] an acronym for sheḥuzot.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:20:1.hebrew: שלא יצא חבל - ראש החבל לא יצא מתחת ידו טפח למטה, דדמי כמי שנושאה בידו, ולא מתחזיא שהיא מאפסר הגמלים:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:20:1.english: That a rope does not extend - The end of the rope shall not extend a handbreadth downward below his hand, for it resembles one who carries it in his hand, and it is not apparent that it is [part] of the camels' halter.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:20:2.hebrew: שמואל - דאמר טפח, לאורויי הלכה למעשה אתא לאשמעינן: דהבא לימלך לפנינו אמרינן ליה טפח, שלא להקל באיסורין. ומיהו, עד טפחיים ליכא איסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:20:2.english: Shmuel - In that he said [one] handbreadth, he came to teach us to instruct [as] practical halakhah: that to one who comes to seek counsel before us, we say to him, “[Only] a handbreadth,” so as not to be lenient with prohibitions. However, up to two handbreadths there is no prohibition.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:2:1.english: That are bound - An expression of “iron fetters”; [meaning] tied.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:2:2.hebrew: ויקרא להם - בעשרים ושתים עיר שנתן שלמה לחירם, משתעי קרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:2:2.english: And he called them - The verse is speaking of the twenty-two cities that Solomon gave to Hiram.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:4:1.english: Ḥomton - [Land that is] salty and cracked.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:4:2.english: Because the leg sinks into it - The foot sinks into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:4:3.hebrew: עד כבלא - פרק התחתון, שקורין קויל"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:4:3.english: Up to the ankle - The lower joint, which they call cheville [ankle].

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:5:1.hebrew: שמכבנין - קושרין בגד סביבו ביום שנולד, שצמרו נקי, ומשמר צמרו שלא יטנף:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:5:1.english: That they cover - They tie a garment around it on the day it is born, when its wool is clean, and [this] preserves its wool so that it does not become soiled.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:5:2.hebrew: מכבנין - על שעושין כמין קרסי מתכת לחבר הבגד, כמו: ״תנתן כבינתי לבתי״ (גיטין דף טו.), נושק"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:5:2.english: They fasten [mekhabnin] - [Named so] because they make a kind of metal clasp to fasten the garment, as in: “Let my clasp [kevinati] be given to my daughter” (Gittin 15a) — nosche [clasp] in Old French.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:5:3.english: For fine wool - To make garments of fine wool from its wool.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:7:1.english: Independently - And not regarding the dispute of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:1.english: And there are those who teach - This [statement] of Shmuel regarding this [baraita]:

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:2.hebrew: כך הלכה - דליבש מותר, ולחלב אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:2.english: That is the halakha - That to dry is permitted, and for milk [it is] forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:3.hebrew: אבל מי מפיס - מי מטיל גורל ומבחין איזו ליבש ואיזו לחלב? והרואה אותם צרורות ליבש אומר דלחלב הוא, ואתי למישרי תרווייהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:3.english: But who casts lots - Who casts lots and distinguishes which [is bound] to dry [the milk] and which [is bound] for milk? And one who sees them bound to dry [the milk] will say that it is for milk, and will come to permit both of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:4.hebrew: כת"ק - דמתני', דשרי בתרוייהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:8:4.english: In accordance with the first tanna - [That is, the first tanna] of the Mishnah, who permits in both [cases].

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:9:1.hebrew: מטולטלת - י"מ פושל"א (רתמת זנב) שתחת זנבו, וי"מ מרדעת. והאחרון נראה בעיני, דאי רצועה שתחת הזנב קשורה ומחוברת לסרגא, ואיך תפול? וטעמא דמתני' משום שמא תפול ומייתי לה הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:9:1.english: A saddlecloth [metultelit] - Some explain [it as] posle (a tail-harness) that is under its tail, and some explain [it as] a pack-saddle [marda’at]. And the latter [explanation] seems [correct] to me, for if [it were] the strap that is under the tail, it is tied and attached to the saddle, so how could it fall? And the reason of the Mishnah is due to [the concern] lest it fall and he will carry it.

Rashi on Shabbat 54a:9:2.hebrew: לא עקוד ולא רגול - מפרשינן בגמ', שעוקדים ידיהם עם רגליהם בכבלים, שלא יברחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 54a:9:2.english: Neither akud nor ragul - We explain in the Gemara that they bind their forelegs with their hind legs with fetters, so that they do not flee.

Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:17:1.hebrew: והתנן אדם מותר עם כולם לחרוש ולמשוך - וא"ת: אפי' יהא אדם נמי אסור, תקשה: דמאי כלאים שייך הכא, כיון שאינו מושך בעגלה ובקרון, דהא בשבת איירי? ואין לומר דאסור להנהיג בכלאים אפי' לא ימשוך שום דבר — דאם כן, יהא אסור להוליך ולהזיז ממקומו שור פסולי המוקדשין, דחשיב כשני מינים, כדאמרי' בפרק בתרא דמכות (דף כב.): "המנהיג בשור פסולי המוקדשין לוקה, גוף אחד הוא ועשאו הכתוב שני גופים". וי"ל, דה"ק: אילימא כלאים דאדם — והא דקתני "ובלבד שלא יכרוך", בחול קאמר, כדאוקימנא לעיל (פ"ב דף כג:) "ולא בשמן שריפה" דאיירי ביו"ט, ומיירי שמושכין שום דבר. אי נמי, י"ל: דחשיב משיכה מה שנושאים שניהם את החבלים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:17:1.english: "Didn't we learn: A person is permitted to plow and to pull with all [animals]" - And if you say: Even if a person were also prohibited, it should be difficult: What [prohibition of] diverse kinds (kilayim) applies here, since he is not pulling a wagon or a cart, for this is discussing Shabbat? And one cannot say that it is prohibited to drive [diverse kinds] even if they do not pull anything; for if so, it would be prohibited to lead and move from its place an ox of disqualified consecrated animals — which is considered like two species, as we say in the last chapter of Makkot (22a): "One who drives an ox of disqualified consecrated animals is lashed; it is one body, but Scripture rendered it two bodies." And one can say that this is what [the Gemara] means: If we say [it is] diverse kinds of man — and that which [the mishna] teaches, "provided that he does not intertwine [the ropes]," refers to a weekday (just as we established earlier [in chapter 2, 23b] regarding "nor with [consecrated] oil [that was defiled and designated for] burning," that it discusses Yom Tov), and it is dealing with [a case where] they are pulling something. Alternatively, one can say that the fact that both of them carry the ropes is considered pulling.

Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:4:1.hebrew: עד כבלא - מפרש ר"י: עד השוק, כדאמר בפ' במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף כג:): "בירית באחת, כבלים בשתים" — שמניחין הכבלים בשוק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:4:1.english: "Up to the ankle [kavla]" - The Ri explains: Up to the shin, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Isha (below, Shabbat 23b [63b]): "A garter [is worn] on one [leg], ankle chains on two" — for they place the ankle chains on the shin.

Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:7:1.hebrew: רב אמר ליבש מותר כו' - וא"ת: לימא מר "הלכה כמר"? וי"ל: משום דאיכא דמפכי להו לתנאי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:7:1.english: "Rav said: To dry is permitted," etc. - And if you say: Let the Master say, "The halakha is in accordance with the Master"? And one can say: Because there are those who reverse [the opinions of] the Tannaim.

Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:8:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יהודה בן בתירא - הא דנקט ר' יהודה בן בתירה ולא נקט ר' יוסי — משום דבמקום שאין עושין כלל אלא כדי ליבש, שרי ר' יהודה בן בתירא, דלא שייך התם מי מפיס; ור' יוסי אוסר, משום דילמא נפיל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:8:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira - That which [Shmuel] cited Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and did not cite Rabbi Yosei is because in a place where they only ever do [so] in order to dry [the milk], Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira permits [it], as "who can determine?" does not apply there; whereas Rabbi Yosei prohibits [it even there], out of concern that [the pouch] might fall off.

Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:8:2.hebrew: <abbr title="רבנו תם">ר"ת</abbr> גריס: "אמר רב: הלכה <abbr title="כתנא קמא">כת"ק</abbr>, ושמואל אמר: כו'", וכן: "כי אתא רבין, <abbr title="אמר רבי">א"ר</abbr> יוחנן: הלכה כתנא קמא". ואתי שפיר "איכא דמתני לה" — לדרב ושמואל דלעיל — אהא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 54a:8:2.english: Rabbeinu Tam reads: “Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with the first tanna, and Shmuel said, etc.,” and similarly: “When Ravin came, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with the first tanna.” And [with this reading,] “there are those who teach it” — [referring] to [the dispute] of Rav and Shmuel from above — “regarding this” [baraita] works out well.
